title: Type deduction for objects using the auto keyword
recap: auto deduces an object type from its initializer. The expression still has its ordinary type: auto does not turn integer division into floating-point division.
Use a clear initializer so the deduced type is intentional. const auto can keep the deduced value immutable without repeating its exact type.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice type deduction for objects using the auto keyword.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement midpoint(low, high) returning their floating-point midpoint, even for odd sums or reversed endpoints. Inputs are between -1000000 and 1000000. Use auto for a local intermediate so its type follows the expression; the tests care about the double result, not how you spell locals.
hints: The midpoint is the sum divided by two.
Choose an expression that preserves half units.
Reversing endpoints should not change the answer.
